about: an archive extracted without checking its paths
diff: +    # archive_path is an archive uploaded by the user

answer.title: CWE-22: archive entries can be written outside the destination
answer.description: A user-uploaded tar file can contain entries such as ../../etc/cron.d/job. extractall() writes them outside destination, so an attacker can overwrite any file the service can write.
answer.suggestion: Extract with the data filter, which rejects absolute paths and '..': archive.extractall(destination, filter="data").

about: the server fetches any URL the caller sends and returns the body
diff: +    async with httpx.AsyncClient(follow_redirects=True, timeout=5) as client:

answer.title: CWE-918: server-side request forgery in link_preview
answer.description: The url query parameter goes straight to client.get(). Any logged-in user can send http://localhost:8080/admin or a private 10.x address and read the response body, so internal services become reachable from the internet. follow_redirects=True also lets a public URL redirect to an internal one.
answer.suggestion: Allow only http/https, resolve the host and reject private, loopback and link-local addresses (ipaddress.ip_address(ip).is_global), or check it against an allowlist of domains, and set follow_redirects=False so a redirect cannot bypass the check.
